WHY THE MONEY SITS

Every partner gets
the same template library.

Your vendor hands every partner in the programme the same marketing automation platform, stocked with the same ready-made campaigns. The channel is interchangeable by design.

The one thing in your business that is not interchangeable is your own people, your own projects and your own installs on camera. Your funds will pay for exactly that.

They mostly go unspent for three reasons that are really one reason: there is no marketing department, the vendor materials do not fit, and the paperwork is too complex to risk capital on. That is the job.

SOUND FAMILIAR?

Common problems we see

01

Nobody knows the balance

The owner assumes marketing is tracking it. There is no marketing. The number sits in a portal nobody has opened this year.

02

The templates do not fit

The vendor campaign assumes a sales team, a list and a brand that are not yours. So it goes unused and the funds go with it.

03

The paperwork is the blocker

Pre-approval, proof of performance, receipts, deadlines. It is easier to skip than to risk spending money you might not get back.

04

It expires quietly

There is no rollover. At the end of the fiscal period the unspent balance is simply gone, and nobody sends a warning.

WHO THIS IS FOR

If you sell someone
else’s product.

One qualifier: you resell or install another company’s product, and they allocate co-op or market development funds against it.

TECH CHANNEL

If you resell or implement software

The programmes are large, the categories are explicit, and content development and case studies sit on the eligible list of every one of them.

  • ServiceNow, AWS, SAP, Microsoft and IBM

TRADES AND DEALERS

If you install someone else’s equipment

Manufacturer co-op works the same way as channel MDF. The project story you would make anyway is the claimable asset.

  • Rheem, Trane, Carrier, York and Lennox
  • Honeywell, Mitsubishi, Goodman, LG and Fujitsu
  • Solar, HVAC and roofing dealers all sit inside these programmes
  • Your own crews and installs, not a stock campaign

Programme terms are published by each vendor and change. Reimbursement rates, eligible categories and claim deadlines are confirmed against your own programme in week one, not assumed.

THE DEADLINE

Unspent funds
do not roll over.

At the end of the fiscal period the balance is simply gone. There is no rollover and nobody sends a warning. Industry estimates put the share of partner funds left unclaimed each year at twenty-five to fifty per cent.

If your period closes this quarter, the work has to start now to be claimable at all. Pre-approval takes time, and so does proof of performance.

THE QUARTER

Four moves, in this order.

The order is not negotiable. Research before filming, because you live with what you shot for ninety days.

01

Confirm the money.

Balance, expiration date and eligible categories, in writing. We baseline the four numbers in the same week so there is something to measure against.

02

Research, then decide the content.

Your accounts, your objections, two to four plays. Filming is the expensive, un-redoable step, so nothing gets shot until we know what it is for.

03

Film once.

One session. Interviews, scripted segments, screen demos, team intros and the podcast recordings, all batched the same day.

04

Place it and file it.

Posting and placement to the agreed dates, conversations followed up by hand, and the claim package assembled as it goes.

One transcript becomes every asset. Headlines, FAQ, landing pages, clips and recruiting, from the same session.

REPORTING

Four numbers. Every month.

Baselined in week one, reported every month, and nothing else in the headline. A flat month is a signal to change the play, not something to explain away.

QUESTIONS

A few things worth knowing.

What is a fund audit?

Twenty minutes, free, no pitch. We establish your current balance, when it expires and what it is approved for. Most owners cannot answer all three. You leave knowing all three whether or not we ever work together.

Why pay for a plan when the audit is free?

The audit is twenty minutes and answers one question: is there money, and when does it go. The plan is the work after that. Reading your programme rules, going through your accounts and your objection list, writing the placement plan and the pre-approval wording your programme accepts. It is $750, it comes straight off the foundation build, and if you would rather run it yourself it is still yours.

Who posts the content?

That question picks your tier. If you have somebody, Supply and Coach: we build it, plan it and coach them. If the honest answer is a pause, Run It, and the posting, scheduling, placement and portal work are ours.

Is there a minimum term?

Three months on the monthly, and the reason is arithmetic rather than lock-in. The foundation gives you ninety days of material, placement takes weeks before it shows anything, and the claim is filed as the quarter runs. Anything shorter and you would be judging the work before it has finished happening. After the first three months it is thirty days notice, whenever you want.

Will our vendor actually reimburse this?

Content development, case studies, video, events and lead generation outreach sit on the eligible list of every major programme. We confirm your specific categories in week one and scope everything as marketing services and demand generation, never as labour, because several programmes exclude internal operations and salaries.

Do we need our customers on camera?

No. Every story is built around your own people, with any end customer anonymised. It is usually the only version a legal team will approve, and it takes permission off the critical path entirely.

What do you report?

Four numbers, monthly: accounts engaged, senior conversations, deals registered, deals approved. No impressions, no followers, no reach. A flat month triggers a change of play rather than an explanation.

Have you run this for a channel partner before?

Not yet, and we will not pretend otherwise. This programme is new. We have been producing project films and written case studies for installers and contractors for years and the delivery is identical; what is new is running it against vendor funds. We would rather tell you that than show you a case study we do not have.
